49.description: Captures whether security is framed as enabling developers through good defaults and reduced friction.

levels.descriptor: Security is framed mainly as control, compliance, or personal interest.
Hints at helping other engineers but vaguely.
Explicitly wants to make secure behavior easier for developers.
Shows strong empathy for busy engineering teams and treats friction reduction as a design goal.

49.name: Education level
49.description: Captures the highest relevant academic credential stated.

levels.descriptor: Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience only.
Master's degree in a relevant field.
Doctoral degree in a relevant field.

49.name: Relevant experience duration
49.description: Captures total years of professional software experience relevant to the posting.

levels.descriptor: Roughly 2 to 3 years of relevant software experience.
Roughly 4 to 5 years of relevant software experience.
6 or more years of relevant software experience.

49.name: Production service scope
49.description: Captures repeated ownership of software tested, maintained, and launched in production.

levels.descriptor: Mentions about 2 production services or similarly limited launch history.
Mentions about 4 services or moderate repeated delivery.
Mentions about 6 or more services or extensive repeated launches.

49.name: Programming language breadth
49.description: Captures breadth of multi-language development beyond Go.

levels.descriptor: Go plus only a small additional set of languages.
Go plus a moderate additional set of languages.
Go plus a wide additional set across many languages.

49.evidence: "Having reviewed the posting closely, I believe my background aligns directly"
49.name: Qualification mapping clarity
49.description: Captures how easy the letter makes it for a reader to verify match against the stated requirements.

levels.descriptor: The reader must infer major qualifications from scattered statements.
Covers some requirements clearly but leaves important fit areas ambiguous.
Makes most core qualifications easy to verify.
Systematically maps experience to the posting with very little ambiguity.

49.name: Python depth
49.description: Captures the depth and concreteness of Python use relevant to automation, services, or tooling.

levels.descriptor: No meaningful Python use is described.
Mentions Python as a secondary tool with little detail.
Shows regular Python use for services, automation, or tooling.
Shows strong production-grade Python ownership with concrete responsibilities or quality markers.

49.name: AI production exposure
49.description: Captures whether the applicant has actually built AI-backed functionality in production.

levels.descriptor: No AI experience is mentioned.
Mentions AI interest or limited experimentation.
Describes building or shipping AI-backed production features.
Shows sustained professional AI work across multiple features, systems, or contexts.

49.evidence: "evaluation scaffolding required to deploy them responsibly"
49.name: AI reliability discipline
49.description: Captures awareness of evaluation, failure modes, and operational controls for AI systems.

levels.descriptor: No sign of evaluation or failure-mode awareness.
Makes only a vague claim that AI was made trustworthy.
Mentions evaluation, constraints, hardening, or dependability concerns.
Demonstrates mature operational thinking about AI through explicit evaluation practices or failure-mode engineering.

49.evidence: "Python agents" "Go services constrain what they may touch"
49.name: Agentic architecture ownership
49.description: Captures hands-on design ownership of agent-based systems with clear boundaries and control planes.

levels.descriptor: No agentic system experience is mentioned.
Mentions agents without explaining design responsibility.
Describes building agentic tooling with defined Python and Go roles.
Shows design ownership of bounded autonomy, permissions, auditing, or task decomposition.

49.name: Vulnerability triage automation
49.description: Captures direct experience automating intake, triage, routing, or deduplication of security findings.

levels.descriptor: No direct triage automation evidence appears.
Expresses interest in reducing manual security toil without claiming prior ownership.
Built automation for intake, routing, or triage of vulnerability reports.
Shows clear ownership of classification, deduplication, routing, or measurable workload reduction.

49.name: Security assessment depth
49.description: Captures how substantive the applicant's security review experience is.

levels.descriptor: No meaningful assessment work is described.
Mentions reviews or assessments only in general terms.
Describes hands-on threat modeling, code review, or formal assessments.
Presents assessments as rigorous engineering work with attacker perspective, findings, and remediation follow-through.

49.evidence: "replaced ad-hoc traversals with proper graph algorithms"
49.name: Algorithmic fluency
49.description: Captures demonstrated command of data structures and algorithms through concrete engineering examples.

levels.descriptor: No concrete algorithms or data-structure evidence is given.
Claims strength in algorithms but gives little proof.
Gives one solid concrete example of algorithmic redesign or structure choice.
Gives especially crisp or multiple examples showing strong algorithmic judgment.

49.name: Security credential strength
49.description: Captures the strength of external security validation named in the letter.

levels.descriptor: No external security credential is named.
Names a baseline credential such as Security+.
Names a hands-on offensive credential such as OSCP or an equivalent practical exam.

49.name: Capture-the-flag intensity
49.description: Captures the seriousness and demonstrated level of offensive practice through CTF participation.

levels.descriptor: No CTF activity is mentioned.
Mentions occasional or casual participation.
Shows regular participation or consistently strong involvement.
Indicates serious competition with near-top or top placements.

49.name: Open-source engagement
49.description: Captures public software contribution ranging from occasional fixes to sustained maintainership.

levels.descriptor: No open-source work is mentioned.
Mentions occasional patches or one-off upstream fixes.
Describes regular contribution or maintainership of an actively used project.
Shows sustained public maintainership with external users, reviews, releases, and community responsibility.

49.evidence: "distributed job scheduler with leader election and crash recovery"
49.name: Personal project rigor
49.description: Captures the ambition and technical depth of self-directed projects described outside the day job.

levels.descriptor: No side project is described, or it is only mentioned in passing.
Describes a small utility or simple application.
Describes a substantial self-directed build with a clear engineering challenge.
Describes an ambitious systems project tackling hard distributed or failure-handling problems.

49.evidence: "queue went from a dreaded chore to something the tooling mostly runs itself"
49.name: Achievement concreteness
49.description: Captures whether accomplishments are presented as specific examples with observable outcomes rather than generic claims.

levels.descriptor: Relies mostly on abstract claims and adjectives.
Includes some specific tasks or tools but little sense of result.
Gives concrete examples of what was built or changed.
Gives concrete examples plus outcomes, design choices, or why the work mattered.

49.name: Security automation framing
49.description: Captures the sophistication with which the letter frames security work as a scaling and systems problem.

levels.descriptor: Treats security work generically or not at all as a systems problem.
Mentions automation as useful but without a strong framing of the problem.
Frames security work in terms of reducing toil, scaling response, or systematizing workflow.
Frames security automation with high sophistication around scarce expert attention, variant analysis, routing, or organization-wide capacity.
